steps.what: Advise patients about recommended treatment, uncertainties and alternatives

tasks.design: Retain the treatment discussion with the practitioner. The clinical record system {OTHER} supplies assessment context, while recommendations, alternatives and uncertainty are explained personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on individual findings and patient preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting technology does not remove the clinical conversation in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Patients may have expectations that do not match the evidence or clinical findings.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner checks understanding and recognises when further assessment or referral is needed.
tasks.altitude: Treatment advice remains the practitioner's responsibility; no time reduction is claimed.

reach.task: Clarify patient goals for a referral
reach.learn: Referral boundaries and shared functional terminology

evidence.claim: Retaining individual treatment advice is an E1 assessment from model knowledge, not a measured productivity claim.

assumptions: Boundary is explaining recommended treatment after assessment, not diagnosis, scheduling or record production.
No structured patient classification or machine action is introduced.
No custom software is proposed; retain existing clinical references and records.
Zero upkeep because the task and tools do not change.
unknowns: Typical clinical complexity and referral arrangements
research_questions: Do patients understand alternatives and know when to seek further assessment after advice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. The clinical conversation stays human; no hypothetical documentation baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel patients about daily habits and wellbeing

steps.what: Counsel patients about nutrition, exercise, sleep and stress within professional scope

tasks.design: Keep counselling and checking understanding with the practitioner. Approved patient information in {DOCS} can support the discussion, with nutrition or mental-health needs referred when outside professional competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Behavioural guidance depends on patient circumstances and willingness to act.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible reference material supports counselling but does not establish a shorter conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Advice must be feasible, evidence-informed and within professional scope.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner notices barriers, avoids inappropriate advice and agrees realistic next actions.
tasks.altitude: Counselling time and professional responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Recognise a need for specialist nutrition referral
reach.learn: Referral criteria and limits of general lifestyle advice

evidence.claim: Thuisarts provides guideline-based patient information; this supports reference availability, not automated personalised counselling or time savings.
Keeping counselling human with zero savings is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is counselling itself; written plan creation would require a separately observed baseline.
No free structured lifestyle profile or automatic advice step is assumed.
Use existing approved references; no new tool or content system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no workflow changes.
unknowns: Patient support needs and referral access
research_questions: Which barriers prevent patients from following agreed advice, and require specialist support?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Conversation and understanding checks retain all their time; reference availability is not a labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide patients through exercises for mobility

steps.what: Select appropriate exercises and demonstrate the movements
Observe patient exercises and correct technique or stop when needed

tasks.design: Keep exercise selection, demonstration and observed correction with the practitioner. Existing instructions in {DOCS} remain supporting references; no model chooses a programme or infers that a patient can perform it safely.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance requires seeing the patient's movement and response.
tasks.enabler_now: Generating generic exercise text does not remove demonstrated teaching work.
tasks.still_hard: Pain, compensatory movement and changing symptoms need contextual assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner adapts or stops an exercise based on observed response.
tasks.altitude: No change to exercise guidance responsibility or time is claimed.

reach.task: Communicate observed functional limitations for referral
reach.learn: Functional assessment terminology and professional boundaries

evidence.claim: Hands-on exercise guidance retains its time in this E1 model-knowledge assessment; the automation prior does not establish a removable paperwork step.

assumptions: Boundary is individual exercise guidance, not producing a booklet or tracking an app programme.
No structured contraindication flag, automated prescription or competence score is assumed.
Existing instruction material suffices; no custom system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because the work remains unchanged.
unknowns: Exercise teaching methods and clinical scope
research_questions: How often must a demonstrated exercise be adapted after observing the patient perform it?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Both selection and observed practice remain human; the task text does not establish manual handout assembly to automate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze radiographs and identify concerns requiring referral

steps.what: Analyze x-rays with patient history and image quality limitations
Assess possible fractures or disease and arrange appropriate clinical referral

tasks.design: Retain radiograph assessment in the image-viewing system {OTHER} and refer uncertainty or concerning findings through established clinical arrangements. The digest's mammography example does not establish capability for spinal radiographs or exclusion of fractures and disease.
tasks.previous_blocker: Image findings require clinical interpretation and recognition of limits.
tasks.enabler_now: No applicable validated imaging capability is established by this digest.
tasks.still_hard: Images may be incomplete or nonspecific; absence of a visible abnormality does not resolve every clinical concern.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner integrates symptoms, image quality and uncertainty and obtains appropriate specialist assessment.
tasks.altitude: Image interpretation responsibility and referral decisions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Provide relevant history and a focused referral question
reach.learn: Imaging limitations and specialist referral requirements

evidence.claim: Transpara flags breast cancer in mammograms; that capability does not validate spinal radiograph analysis or fracture exclusion.
Retaining the described interpretation and referral work is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is review of already-acquired images and deciding on referral; acquisition and specialist interpretation are outside the focal baseline.
The image-viewing system is {OTHER}. No machine interpretation or structured normal-result contract is assumed.
Do not commission custom image interpretation; existing viewing and clinical referral arrangements remain.
Zero upkeep because no change is introduced. Local professional scope and national rules require customer confirmation.
unknowns: Authorised imaging scope and specialist review arrangements
research_questions: Which findings and uncertainties require specialist image review under local practice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Clinical image assessment and referral judgement retain all time; unrelated mammography results supply no labour estimate.

reach: Clarify functional goals for physical therapy referral
